label: copy phase of length-9 sequences, echoing m/t/k/d/x
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never on original tokens or <DEL>), almost entirely in long sequences: L=9 holds 87% of activation mass and L>=8 holds 99%. Never fires on the first occurrence of a token. Within that window the rate depends on the input token: m (7.5x lift), t, k, d and x are strongest, with r, e and 1 weaker. Rate is highest at the last two copy steps (t=16,17, up to 14% of steps), with a second bump at recall_idx 2-3. Copy phase of L=9 alone gives recall 0.83 but precision 0.08. Adding the token set raises dev F1 to about 0.37 (precision 0.30, mass recall 0.59). Output-token conditions (h, i, m, j) did not help. Magnitude is small (max 0.018), and the top activations are at late copy steps of L=9 on k/t/m/d/e inputs. It looks like a distributed content code in long-sequence copying, not a clean single concept.
